basis: Absence of major brain structures and the cranial vault defines anencephaly; adrenal hypoplasia is frequent (30-79%).

decisions.musculoskeletal: primary: absence of the cranial vault is a defining skeletal malformation of anencephaly.

basis: The supplied definition specifies cardiomyopathy caused by selenium deficiency together with Coxsackievirus; the mineral deficiency supports the metabolic axis.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: selenium deficiency is a defining nutritional mineral disorder underlying the cardiomyopathy.

basis: Coagulation deficiency with defining recurrent venous thrombosis; retinal and destructive skin findings chiefly reflect severe recessive disease, not most across this umbrella.

decisions.cardiovascular: primary: recurrent venous thrombosis is explicitly part of the disease definition, beyond a future vascular risk.

basis: Inherited oxalate-handling disorder with hyperoxaluria and calcium oxalate stones; obstruction and acute kidney injury are documented in the reported patient.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: the inherited oxalate-handling abnormality is supported by hyperoxaluria in 1/1 reported patients, beyond the gene name alone.

basis: Hyperinsulinemic hypoglycemia; persistent developmental disability and atrial septal defect each occur in 1/1 assessed, at least 1/3 known patients (~33%); evidence is sparse.

decisions.cardiovascular: involved: atrial septal defect is structural cardiac disease documented in one of three known patients (~33%); the estimate remains uncertain.

basis: Hypomyelinating neuropathy with congenital contractures; pulmonary hypoplasia occurs in 3/9 (~33%). Ocular findings in one assessed patient do not establish common involvement.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis and strabismus are documented in one assessed patient among at least nine known; a frequency of >=30% is not established.

basis: FAH deficiency causes defining liver disease and renal tubulopathy; porphyria-like neuropathic crises affect roughly 40% of untreated patients. Rickets is occasional.

decisions.neurologic: involved: direct peripheral and autonomic neuropathic crises affect roughly 40% of untreated patients and are characteristic of the disease.

basis: Congenital dystroglycan glycosylation disorder with muscular dystrophy and intellectual disability; myopia affects 3/5 (60%). Cardiomyopathy and cataracts occur in 5-29%.

decisions.metabolic_endocrine: primary: defective O-mannosyl glycosylation of dystroglycan constitutes an inborn glycosylation disorder, supported by the disease ancestry.

basis: The supplied definition describes actual familial rhabdoid tumors; CNS and kidney are tumor-origin sites, each documented in 1/2 patients.

decisions.renal: primary: renal rhabdoid tumor is a tumor-origin manifestation of the defined familial tumor syndrome, documented in 1/2 patients.

basis: Renal cysts cause progressive kidney damage. Liver cysts are common (>70% of adults with dominant PKD) but usually preserve function; hepatic fibrosis chiefly defines recessive PKD.

decisions.hepatic: none: common dominant-PKD liver cysts usually preserve function; damaging hepatic fibrosis chiefly affects the less common recessive subtype.
